items.definition: To do the same game with another child, side by side. It is the simplest friendship there is.
items.example: We play together at break time every day.

items.definition: A child you have just met. Saying hello twice makes a new child feel welcome.
items.example: I have a new friend in class 4B.

items.definition: The question word that asks for a thing or an idea. It is the most useful question word of all.
items.example: What does this word mean?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a person.
items.example: Who is your new teacher?

items.definition: Introduces the conditions on a and b.
items.example: ax + b = 0, where a is non-zero.

items.definition: At the time when something happens.
The question word that asks for a reason. Why questions are the most interesting ones.
items.example: Why do we have to sleep?

items.definition: The question word that asks for a way of doing something.
items.example: How do you spell your name?

items.definition: A hot, upset feeling. It often comes fast and shows in your hands and face.
items.example: I feel angry, so I am going to count to ten.

items.definition: A smaller angry feeling that comes when something still will not work.
items.example: I am frustrated with this puzzle.

items.definition: To bring your body back to quiet so you can think and speak.
items.example: Let us calm down first, then talk.

items.definition: To take air in slowly and let it out slowly.
items.example: Breathe in, and blow out slowly.

items.definition: To have or use a thing with others.
To play first and then let the next person play.
items.example: We take turns on the slide.

items.definition: To stay calm and do something else until your turn comes.
items.example: I wait until my friend finishes the puzzle.

items.definition: To give one thing away and get a different thing back.
items.example: I trade my ball for your dinosaur.

items.definition: The polite word you say after somebody helps you or gives you something.
items.example: Thank you for lending me your ruler.

items.definition: The word you say when you did something wrong. It shows you take responsibility.
items.example: Sorry, I stepped on your foot.

items.definition: The polite way to get somebody's attention or to pass by them.
items.example: Excuse me, may I get past?

items.definition: A careful, grown-up way to ask for something. People listen more when you use it.
items.example: May I sit here, please?

items.definition: Something that happens inside you. It shows on your face and tells you what you need.
items.example: My feeling today is happy.

items.definition: A warm, good feeling inside. It makes you want to smile and share.
items.example: I feel happy when my friend sits with me.

items.definition: A heavy feeling inside. It often wants tears or quiet time.
items.example: I feel sad because my cat is away.

items.definition: An afraid feeling. Your heart beats fast and you want to run or hide.
items.example: I feel scared in the dark, so I hold my blanket.

items.definition: A part of a plant that holds seeds and is good to eat, like a mango or a pear.
items.example: A mango and a pear are both fruit.

items.definition: Ready to eat, sweet and soft. A green mango is not ripe yet.
items.example: This banana is yellow and ripe.

items.definition: The outside skin of a fruit. You usually peel it before eating.
items.example: I peel the orange before I eat it.

items.definition: A tiny helper in food that keeps your body working well. Fruit has plenty of vitamins.
items.example: One orange gives me lots of vitamin C.

items.definition: A place where milk is cleaned, heated and packed into bottles and cartons.
items.example: Our milk comes from the dairy near the town.

items.definition: The bag under a cow's body where the milk is made.
items.example: The farmer washes the cow's udder before milking.

items.definition: Heated quickly to kill tiny germs, so the milk stays safe to drink.
items.example: This milk is pasteurised, so it is safe to drink.

items.definition: A mineral from food that makes your bones and teeth strong.
items.example: Milk is full of calcium, and calcium keeps my bones strong.

items.definition: A measure of liquid. There are 1000 millilitres in one litre.
items.example: I drink one litre of milk every week.

items.definition: A small amount of food that you eat between two meals.
items.example: I brought a snack to school for break time.

items.definition: To deal with something in a particular way.
The part of food your body cannot digest. It helps your tummy work and keeps you full.
items.example: Wholemeal bread has more fibre than white bread.

items.definition: The building material of your body. It helps you grow and keeps you full for longer.
items.example: Eggs are full of protein, so they are a good snack.

items.definition: The same operation has been applied to both sides.
items.example: The equation stays balanced if you add the same number to both sides.

items.definition: A plant we eat for the part that is not the seed, like a carrot or a cabbage.
items.example: Broccoli and carrot are both vegetables.

items.definition: The part of a plant that grows down into the soil, to hold it up and drink water.
items.example: The root drank the rain deep in the ground.
